subject: Edge demarcation & NAT hairpin validation for ACME private deployment
messages:
From: Tiago Ramos <tiago@cloudconsults.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME on-prem — edge demarc + NAT hairpin pre-check

Evelyn / Jonas / team,

Attaching the preliminary egress matrix and a schematic from the colo for ACME's private deployment. The two items we'd like Redwood to validate before the handoff:

- NAT hairpin (internal->edge->internal) behavior when requests traverse the control plane for telemetry/KMS calls. Does Redwood expect hairpin to the same public IP or to a dedicated internal SNAT?
- BGP handoff: current design uses static eBGP peering to ACME transit. We flagged a split-horizon DNS requirement for model fetch endpoints and want confirmation on route preference (local-pref vs community).
- Packet inspection / firewall: ACME will perform source NAT at the edge. We need to confirm session affinity expectations for streaming tokens (long-lived).

Attachments: acme-egress-matrix-v1.xlsx, schematic-edge-nat.png

Can we get a short validation note (bullet list) and a runbook stub we can hand to ACME NetOps? Happy to join a 30–60m call next week.

Thanks,
Tiago Ramos
CloudConsults — Network Delivery
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tiago Ramos <tiago@cloudconsults.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME on-prem — edge demarc + NAT hairpin pre-check

Hi Tiago — thanks for the artifacts, received. Quick clarifying questions before we produce a validation note: 

1) For KMS calls: will ACME require TLS termination at their edge (TLS passthrough to our control plane) or will they terminate and re-encrypt to our control plane? This changes whether we see source IPs from the client or from ACME SNAT.
2) Do they plan to hairpin to the same public IP (SNAT at the edge) or maintain a distinct internal SNAT pool on the colo (recommended)?
3) Streaming token sessions: expected maximum idle time before state GC? We need this to set session timeouts on the proxy.

I'll draft a short runbook (runbook-egress-validation.md) and an action checklist. Jonas — can you propose the BGP community/local-pref recommendation for ACME so we can include it? Irene / Kimberly — any operational constraints we should call out (observability, audit logs, KMS key rings)?

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Network Ops - ACME <netops@acmegen.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Tiago Ramos <tiago@cloudconsults.io>
Date: 2026-05-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME on-prem — edge demarc + NAT hairpin pre-check

Evelyn / Tiago — quick answers from NetOps: 

- KMS: ACME will terminate TLS at the edge and re-encrypt to the control plane. We will SNAT to a dedicated pool (10.240.8.0/27) for all outbound control-plane-originated traffic.
- Hairpin: We prefer SNAT at the edge (hairpin to same public IP) for legacy apps, but we can publish an internal SNAT pool for new tenants. 
- Streaming sessions: typical idle timeout is 15m; we can extend to 45m for the rollout window if needed.

We'll attach the firewall policy later today and are OK with a 1-hour call to walk through routes.

—ACME NetOps (on behalf of SRE)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Network Ops - ACME <netops@acmegen.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Tiago Ramos <tiago@cloudconsults.io>
Date: 2026-05-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME on-prem — edge demarc + NAT hairpin pre-check

Thanks for the fast responses — consolidating recommended approach below so we have a single handoff artifact. Evelyn, feel free to paste this into the runbook.

Validation summary / recommended config (high level):

- NAT: Accept ACME's dedicated SNAT pool (10.240.8.0/27) for control-plane egress. For long-term, recommend they deploy an internal SNAT pool per tenant to reduce connection churn across shared IPs.
- Hairpin behavior: Support both modes; configure proxy to honor X-Forwarded-For when present and enable hairpin routing rules for models endpoint (prefix /models/). Add a fallback path that preserves session affinity via TCP-level sticky sessions.
- BGP: Set local-pref on Redwood side to prefer eBGP learned routes for model fetch traffic. Request ACME to tag customer-specific prefixes with community 65000:100 to allow easy acceptance on their side. Provide sample bgp-policy-examples.txt (attached).
- DNS: Split-horizon required for model endpoints. ACME should return internal addresses for <model>.redwood-inference.local when requests originate from the colo. Add a short test plan in the runbook to validate resolution and hairpin.
- Security / Observability: Ensure edge firewall preserves source port when SNAT occurs; instrument logs for SNAT pool allocation and correlate with token/session IDs. Provide an audit job to sample logs for first 48 hours after cutover.

Action items / owners: 
- ACME NetOps: share firewall policy and confirm SNAT pool (NETOPS-4123) — due 2026-05-24.
- Redwood (Jonas): produce BGP examples + route-map snippet — due 2026-05-23 (attached).
- Redwood (Irene): add observability checks for SNAT mapping and session affinity — due 2026-05-25.
- Evelyn: finalize runbook and schedule cutover call (30–60m) with ACME + CloudConsults — target week of 2026-05-31.

Attachments: bgp-policy-examples.txt (Jonas), runbook-egress-validation.md (Evelyn)

I'll set up a calendar invite once we have the final firewall policy.

Jonas Weber
Principal Network Architect
Redwood Inference
